Hi Dana and team,

Kicking off prep for the October 18 QBR. Attached is a draft QBR packet and the usage export for September. High level asks from our side:

- Confirm top three areas you want exec attention on (performance, cost, roadmap).
- Any change to the expected renewal cadence or procurement owner?
- Point people for the 30-minute exec review (we suggest Dana + Head of Engineering).

Preliminary notes from our health assessment (see packet):
- Adoption: active seats up 22% month-over-month, but daily inference calls show a 12% tail of high-latency requests concentrated on long-context endpoints.
- Quality: a handful of regressions logged in late Sep against prompt set alpha-helion-11; we flagged two prompts for follow-up.
- Finance: usage variance vs forecast is +18% (over target), procurement signaled potential budget squeeze for Q1 2028.

Attachments: HelionAI_QBR_Packet_v1.pdf, usage_export_202709.csv

Proposed next steps: internal sync with Jordan and Marcus today; follow-up with your procurement lead by Wednesday; final QBR deck by Friday end of day.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Thanks Stephanie. Quick context from our side:

- Attendees: I will attend; I am coordinating with Mateo (Head of Engineering) and Laila (Head of Procurement) to join the exec slot.
- Budget: finance is tightening in calendar Q1 2028 due to a corporate freeze; Procurement asked for a 15% reduction target across platform vendors. That is the principal risk to renewal.

For data points, attaching our internal export and the security questionnaire response for reference. We want the QBR to surface: 1) mitigation plan for latency, 2) cost optimization levers, and 3) roadmap alignment on long-context improvement.

On Mon, Oct 4, 2027 at 09:30 AM PDT, Dana Park wrote:
> Thanks Stephanie. Quick context from our side: ...

Dana, thanks for the context and the incident pointer. Proposed mitigation plan (short list):

1) Immediate (48-72 hours): enable a targeted autoscale policy for the long-context model endpoint plus a hotfix to reduce KV cache pressure on large-sequence requests. This will reduce observed tail latency.
2) Short term (2 weeks): deploy a tuned kernel for the reasoning model (Q4 runtime patch) and push a config that favors per-request KV cache persistence for high-memory queries.
3) Commercial: offer a one-time bounded usage credit of up to 10% on the Sept invoice to offset the procurement request while we demonstrate latency improvements.

I will run the 48-hour plan with infra tomorrow AM and update with expected metrics. Jordan, we will provide an estimated cost of the autoscale delta for your revenue slide.

Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
marcus.lin@redwood.com
